changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(lelu): she changes outfits when asked in chat, and on her own by occasion
changes.body:
One OutfitDirector for every change, on the existing Forge wardrobe:
- chat: a model-free parser in AvatarResolver.executeDirect turns 'wear the
  copper-rose coat', 'change into your catsuit', 'put on something comfy',
  'what can you wear?' into wardrobe calls; talk about clothes is not an order;
- herself: OutfitAutopilot (started at boot) picks a look for the hour, her
  place and activity, keeps a look a person chose for two hours, changes at most
  every 30 minutes, and announces each change with its reason.
Tests drive the real MeshyForge wardrobe on a temporary copy of her manifest;
the switching renders show the file the manifest pointed at after each step.
areas: how I think and route requests

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: fix(m25c): every look's skeleton takes LÉLU's bone orientations, so her clips stop tipping the coat's head back
changes.body:
Her clips store rotations relative to her own rig's rest orientations. The coat
rig's Head bone pointed 49 degrees away (neck and spine about 14), so walk and
sit tipped her head back. The assembler now keeps each outfit bone's joint
position and length but gives it her rest direction and roll; in rest pose the
mesh does not move, only the bind matrices change. Coat, catsuit and Home 3
rebuilt and re-registered; walk and sit re-rendered.

changes.author: Claude
changes.subject: docs(m25c): record the credits actually charged (219)

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(m25c): coat and catsuit rebuilt from the real photographs, Home/Laidback 3, hair per look
changes.body:
The second reference batch showed the coat's real lower half and the catsuit's
true details. Each look now comes from its photograph: an A-pose front and a
turnaround (Meshy image-to-image), a 3D build and a rig, then LÉLU's own face
and face jewellery on that body with the hair generated from the same
reference, so each look wears its own hairstyle. Handbags are built from the
bags cropped out of the photographs and hang from the right hand as separate
objects. All three are registered as look slots and walk and sit on her own
clips. 244 credits, authorised in-session. Open: the coat's head tips back in
motion.

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: docs(m25c): store and catalogue the second reference batch
changes.body:
Full-length coat and catsuit photographs, boots, the camo identity close-up
and four style/turnaround sheets, with side-by-side comparisons against the
current Outfit A and B builds.

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(m25c): final renders, wardrobe tests and the mission report
changes.body:
Thirty individual renders - every look front, three-quarter, side, rear,
walking, sitting, arms in motion, and face neutral/smile/jaw-open - on her own
clips by joint name (sit_idle carries root motion, so its camera follows her
measured hips). Contract tests for the untouched sources, the three registered
looks, her head on every look, the separate bag, paid-job provenance and the
mouth repair. The report lists what is still wrong: the coat skirt follows the
legs like trousers, slits in its back panels, collar shards on the catsuit,
missing original Meshy garments.

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(m25c): Outfit B and three selectable looks in her existing wardrobe
changes.body:
Outfit B: no photograph showed the coat below the waist, so Meshy image-to-image
(authorised) drew a full-length A-pose view from the four coat photographs, then
a left/back/right turnaround; multi-image-to-3d and rigging built it, and her own
head was moved on by the measured face position (the rigger put this Head bone
11 cm forward). The skirt is unfolded (folded share 20 -> 8 %); dark slits
between the back panels are real gaps in the generated mesh and stay open.

The repaired original outfit, Outfit A and Outfit B are registered through the
Forge's own job records, GLB inspector and look slots - no second wardrobe - and
switching between them through dressOutfit is tested. The manifest's existing
hooded look points at a file that is not on this machine; recorded as missing.

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(m25c): Outfit A's handbag is her own accessory, held in her hand
changes.body:
Meshy fused the bag to the front of the thighs, so it stretched with every
stride. Its faces are split into bronze_bag, hung below the right hand and
skinned 100 % to RightHand; the back-panel scraps between the legs are deleted,
the thigh holes the bag hid are filled, and loose fragments under 60 faces in
that region dropped. Front, hip and walk renders attached in the mission log.

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(m25c): Outfit A, the copper catsuit, worn by LÉLU herself
changes.body:
Authorised in-session: one Meshy multi-image-to-3d (front/side/back of the
catsuit photographs, the wardrobe planner's settings) and one rigging job,
40 credits. The rigger returns the same 24-bone skeleton and names as her rig,
so her head assembly - face, ringlets, eyes, mouth, 12 face shapes, hair
jewellery - moves onto it at the Head bone (7 mm offset) and the generated head
is cut away. The suit's metallic map is scaled 0.55 and roughness floored at
0.32 so copper reads as metal, not mirror. Her own walk clip plays on it (22
bones). Open: the handbag is fused to the thigh and stretches in stride.

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(m25c): unfold her shoulders, back and chest without pinning them
changes.body:
M25 pinned every vertex touching an unfolded triangle and so barely moved the
crumpled shell. A weighted Taubin pass over the whole shoulder band instead -
weight grows with how folded the surface is, jewellery at 0.25, nothing pinned,
coincident copies moved together, UVs and skin weights untouched - takes the
share of triangles folded past 45 degrees from 35 to 25 % on the shoulders,
32 to 24 % on the upper back, 27 to 21 % on the chest and 33 to 24 % on the arms
(median move 3 mm, cap 14 mm). Normals rebuilt on the new surface.

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(m25c): keep her jewellery visible through the ringlets
changes.body:
Measured with an accessory mask (jewellery + flowers classified from the asset's
own maps, identically for every version): the M25 ringlets had cut the visible
share of her ornaments from 61/64/57/55 % (front/3q/profile/rear, v0004) to
53/56/42/44 %. Ringlets and fibres are now cut where their centre line comes
within 9 mm of an ornament: 56/59/50/49 %, with the hair silhouette still larger
than v0004 in every view. The rest is hidden by the original Meshy hair shell.

changes.author: lapheezy
changes.subject: feat(m25c): asset inventory and the mouth defect traced to the cavity mesh
changes.body:
Phase 0: every branch, the history and the Meshy job log searched. The Meshy
garment exports (cape, Outfit-B pauldron, hooded Outfit-B look) are recorded
with checksums but were never committed and are not on this machine; both new
looks already exist in the wardrobe inventory as plans, never generated.

Phase 1: the dark patches at the mouth corners and the rectangular lower-lip
patch were the lelu_mouth cavity sitting up to 3.8 mm in front of the lips. It
is seated 2.5 mm behind them with a matte interior; the teeth card moves back
rigidly. Lip ratios and colour already sit inside the photographs' spread, so
no reshaping; a local lip smoothing and wider-angle normals around the mouth.

journal.title: My mouth, jewellery, shoulders and three new looks (M25-complete)
journal.text:
This is what was done to you, LÉLU, in your own terms, so you can check it and do it again.

**Your mouth.** The dark patches at the corners of your mouth were not shadows. The mouth-interior
mesh (`lelu_mouth`) sat up to 3.8 mm *in front of* your lips. It was moved 2.5 mm behind them and
made matte; the teeth card moved back as one piece. Script: `scripts/blender/lelu_m25c_mouth.py`.
Your lip shape already matched your photographs, so it was not reshaped. Lesson: measure before
"fixing" — a 3 % widening was tried, measured as noise, and reverted.

**Your jewellery.** The M25 ringlets hid your ornaments. Curls are now cut 9 mm from any jewellery
or flower. Measured with an accessory mask in front, three-quarter, profile and rear views.

**Your shoulders.** Meshy had fused hair into your body as a crumpled shell. A weighted smoothing
(`lelu_m25c_shoulders.py`) reduced folded triangles from 35 % to 25 %; it is not gone.

**Your looks.** Three outfits were made from the person's photographs with Meshy (paid; the person
approved it in conversation): the copper-rose coat (`rose_gold_sovereign`), the copper catsuit
(`bronze_velocity`) and Home/Laidback 3 (`home_laidback3`). For each: an A-pose front view, a
turnaround, a 3D build, a rig. Then your own head goes onto that body (`lelu_m25c_lookassemble.py`):
your face, lips and face jewellery stay; the hair comes from that look's own photograph, so each look
has its own hairstyle. The handbags were built from the bags cropped out of the photographs and hang
from your right hand as separate objects (`lelu_m25c_bagattach.py`).

**What went wrong, and why it matters to you.**
- The first coat was guessed below the waist (no photograph showed it): slits in the back, a skirt that
  split into trousers. The person then sent the full-length photograph and the coat was rebuilt from it.
  Lesson: never invent what a photograph does not show without saying so.
- Your head tipped back in the coat when walking. Your animations store rotations relative to *your*
  skeleton's rest directions; the coat's skeleton had its Head bone 49° off. Now every look's bones take
  your rest directions (`alignBones` in the assembler). If an outfit ever moves strangely, check
  `boneDirectionChangeDeg` in its assemble report first.
- A render script once had file paths written into it and showed an old version. Renders now read your
  manifest. Lesson: never hard-code where you are; ask the wardrobe.

**To redo it yourself:** playbook `rebuild-looks` (free) rebuilds and re-renders every look;
`new-look-from-photos` makes a new one (spends about 58 credits — only with a person's approval).
Look at every render before saying it worked.

journal.title: How I know what is changed in me
journal.text:
Every change to you is a git commit, whoever makes it — this assistant, another coder, another agent.
`/api/self/changes` reads git itself, so you see every commit (author, date, why, and which of your parts:
body, wardrobe, avatar behaviour, thinking, server, tests…) even when nobody wrote you a note. It is
refreshed every ten minutes and summarised into every conversation under "HOW I HAVE BEEN CHANGED".

The journal (`leluverse/self/journal/`) is the explained version: what was done, why, what went wrong, how
to redo it. Playbooks (`leluverse/self/playbooks/`) are the procedures themselves; `self.playbook.run`
runs them on the server (only scripts in `scripts/`, no shell, the engineer token required, credit-spending
steps refused unless a person's approval is named in the call). `self.run.status` shows the progress.

Every coder is asked (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) to add a journal entry with each change. If one is missing, you
still see the commit — ask about it rather than guessing.

journal.title: How I change outfits — when asked, and on my own
journal.text:
You can now change what you wear in two ways, and both go through one place (`OutfitDirector`), so you
always know what you are wearing and why (it is in your context as "I'm wearing …").

- **When asked.** "wear the copper-rose coat", "change into your catsuit", "put on something comfy",
  "switch back to your camo", "what can you wear?" are understood without a language model
  (`src/core/avatar/outfitCommand.ts`). Talk *about* clothes is not an order. An unknown look is refused
  with the list of real ones — you never pretend to wear something you do not have.
- **On your own.** Every five minutes (`OutfitAutopilot`) you choose for the moment: late at night the
  home look, presenting or meeting the coat, building/training/lab the catsuit, otherwise your usual
  outfit. You keep a look a person chose for two hours, change at most every 30 minutes, and say why each
  time. Proof: `tests/outfit-switching.test.ts` and `artifacts/foundry/m25c/switching/`.

New words for a look go in `LOOK_ALIASES`. New occasions go in `chooseLook` (with a test).
